verdicts.flaw_description: The purchase counts "cover the sessions that signed in" while "a quarter of each segment never signed in," so the 4-7 percent gains are measured on a subset that excludes a quarter of sessions, not on purchases generally as the claim asserts. (The price clause is neutralized - prices matched the earlier period "to the nearest cent" - so the coverage gap is the live problem.)

The particulate figures "cover the scheduled runs that returned a reading" while "a quarter of scheduled runs at each stack returned no reading," so the 8-14 percent reductions rest on a self-selected three quarters of runs and the missing quarter could sit anywhere. (The throughput halving is defused by the "fixed duty cycle" clause; the missing readings are not defused by anything.)

The abduction averages "cover the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic" while "a quarter of each intake missed the follow-up clinic," so the 9-16 degree gains describe only the three quarters who returned - plausibly the better-recovering ones - not the intakes the claim is about. (The corticosteroid confounder is closed off: injections "held level with the earlier quarter.")

Germination "rates cover the trays that reached the scoring date" while "about a fifth of each lot's trays went unscored," so the 6-11 point gains are computed on the surviving four fifths and exclude precisely the trays most likely to have failed. (The four-degree warmer house air is neutralized by the sealed cabinets "held at a set temperature"; the unscored trays are not.)
